MU.thesis: Micron is riding a genuine AI-driven HBM/DRAM supercycle with sold-out capacity and pricing power, but a violent 30%+ correction, heavy insider selling, and looming 2027-28 supply-glut risk from SK Hynix/Chinese competition warrant caution despite still-rising estimates.
red_flags: CEO sold $37.3M in stock with no open-market purchases in 6 months
~$44.2M total insider selling in July 2026
Chinese competitors (CXMT) and SK Hynix capex surge raising 2027-28 oversupply risk
Customer concentration in AI/hyperscaler demand
Stock down >30% from June highs on AI-valuation and competition fears
catalysts: Q4 FY2026 earnings (record revenue/EPS guidance already given)
HBM4 ramp progress tied to Nvidia Vera Rubin platform
Additional multi-year strategic customer agreements/price-floor contracts
Capacity expansion updates (NY, Idaho, Taiwan, Japan, Singapore, India)
Signs of DRAM/NAND supply-demand gap narrowing or widening into 2027

WDC.thesis: WDC is the pure-play AI cold-storage beneficiary riding a supply-constrained HDD upcycle with expanding margins and sharply rising estimates, though customer concentration and rich valuation temper the risk/reward.
red_flags: hyperscaler customer concentration
insider selling amid rally
stock trading above several analyst price targets / priced for perfection
cyclical HDD pricing risk if supply normalizes
catalysts: Q4 FY26 earnings Aug 5, 2026 vs guided $3.65B rev/$3.25 EPS
HAMR 30TB+ qualification progress
multi-year hyperscaler agreements through 2028
continued HDD supply tightness/pricing into 2027

NBIS.thesis: Nebius is riding a supply-constrained, early-stage AI-cloud infrastructure buildout with massive contracted backlog and Nvidia's strategic backing, though heavy capex, dilution, and customer concentration temper near-term risk.
red_flags: equity/convertible dilution to fund ~$20B+ capex
customer concentration in Microsoft/Meta contracts
high non-cash accrual ratio (126%) inflating GAAP earnings
60x+ forward sales valuation with ~21% short interest
catalysts: Aug 12 Q2 2026 earnings
Vera Rubin NVL72 rollout across US/EMEA in H2 2026
Aug 25 AGM capital structure vote
Nvidia 9.3% stake reinforcing ecosystem validation

IESC.thesis: IES Holdings is riding a genuine mid-cycle grid/data-center capex supercycle with 40% revenue growth, expanding margins, and a backlog up 91% YoY, though insider selling and stretched valuation warrant discipline.
red_flags: Heavy insider selling by Executive Chairman and directors with no offsetting buys
Valuation far above historical/intrinsic value estimates (GF Value ~180% premium)
Residential segment margin/revenue weakness dragging consolidated results
Thin sell-side analyst coverage increasing estimate volatility
Generic customer concentration risk factor in filings despite no single customer >10% of revenue
catalysts: Backlog conversion of $4.5B (+91% YoY) into revenue over coming quarters
2-for-1 stock split effective August 21, 2026 improving liquidity/retail access
Continued AI/data-center power infrastructure capex supercycle
Further bolt-on M&A following Gulf Island Fabrication acquisition
Potential new analyst coverage initiations given rapid market cap growth to ~$14.9B

STRL.thesis: STRL is the purest small/mid-cap play on AI-driven data center and grid-adjacent electrical buildout, with explosive backlog growth and repeated upward estimate revisions outweighing rich valuation and hyperscaler-concentration risk.
red_flags: Hyperscaler/customer concentration in a few large projects
CEO succession planning underway (Cutillo contract to 2027, successor RSUs)
Premium valuation (~63x P/E vs ~40x peers) vulnerable to multiple compression
2027-2028 AI capex digestion risk could compress outer-year backlog conversion
catalysts: Q2 2026 earnings Aug 3, 2026 with conference call Aug 4
Continued CEC electrical integration driving cross-sell backlog growth
Big Tech (Microsoft/Meta/Google/Amazon) capex commentary holding or raising
Further semiconductor fab and hyperscaler project wins expanding $3.8B+ backlog

BE.thesis: Bloom is the fastest-deployable on-site power solution for AI data centers, riding a genuine multi-year capacity/demand super-cycle with rising estimates, though customer concentration and backlog-quality disputes warrant position sizing discipline.
red_flags: 73% single-customer revenue concentration (H1 2026)
Backlog ($20B) vastly exceeds audited RPO (~$492M), per short-seller analysis
Heavy related-party revenue via Brookfield JVs (~74% of Q4'25 revenue)
Oracle Project Jupiter facing permit/pipeline delays
Hunterbrook short-seller allegations on scandium supply chain and performance guarantees
Share dilution from convertible notes and Oracle warrant exercise
Insider selling amid stock volatility
catalysts: Backlog-to-revenue conversion and RPO growth in coming quarters
New hyperscaler/neocloud customer wins beyond Oracle diversifying concentration
Manufacturing capacity scale-up toward 2GW (2026) and stated 25GW long-term visibility
Deployment of Brookfield's $25B AI infrastructure financing framework
Resolution of Hunterbrook allegations / regulatory scrutiny outcome
Progress on Oracle Project Jupiter permitting and first-power timeline

OUST.thesis: OUST is riding a genuine platform-cycle inflection (Rev8 + Stereolabs Physical AI stack) reinforced by a rare regulatory moat from the NDAA Hesai ban, with estimates and price targets moving sharply higher despite recent dilution risk.
red_flags: Recent $200M dilutive equity raise priced at a discount
Persistent EPS misses/integration costs despite revenue beats
Moat and TAM expansion heavily dependent on NDAA Section 164/BABA policy enforcement holding
Rich valuation (~15x P/S) leaves little room for execution missteps

NDAA Section 164 full enforcement (Hesai ban) effective June 30, 2026
Rev8 BABA Act compliance opening state/local infrastructure procurement
Stereolabs integration synergies and cross-sell into robotics/defense
New autonomy partnerships (e.g., AIM Intelligent Machines) expanding robotics TAM

CGNX.thesis: Cognex is entering an early AI-vision platform upcycle (OneVision, In-Sight 6900/3900) with accelerating revenue, margin inflection, and upward estimate revisions, but stretched valuation and auto/logistics concentration cap conviction.
red_flags: auto/logistics customer concentration (~52% of revenue)
new CEO since mid-2025 still executing strategic pivot
premium valuation (~40-75x forward P/E) priced for perfection
China exposure amid rising domestic competitors like Hikvision

OneVision adoption scaling beyond 100+ pilot customers to broad multi-site rollout
New AI hardware launches (In-Sight 6900/3900) driving refresh cycle
Potential M&A deployment of $600M+ cash balance

TER.thesis: Teradyne's blowout momentum is being driven almost entirely by AI-era semiconductor test demand, not by its comparatively small and growth-uncertain Robotics segment, diluting the pure robotics thesis despite excellent overall fundamentals.

Customers pursuing dual-vendor qualification strategies erodes semi-test switching-cost moat
Quarter-to-quarter gross margin volatility tied to product/customer mix
Cyclical dependence on semiconductor capital spending
China export-control and geopolitical exposure

Tokyo Electron UltraFLEXplus/Prexa SDP integrated test partnership ramp
Potential Nvidia GPU wafer-sort testing qualification

2027 realization of share gains from ongoing customer qualifications

HWM.thesis: Howmet's near-monopoly position in next-gen jet engine components plus surging high-margin spares demand is driving durable beat-and-raise growth across a multi-year aerospace/defense supercycle.
red_flags: customer concentration in Boeing/Airbus/engine OEMs
notable insider selling (EVP Marchuk)
premium valuation with high debt load
earnings tightly coupled to OEM build-rate execution
catalysts: continued LEAP/GTF engine ramp driving spares mix toward 20% of revenue
F-35 and legacy fighter defense demand
industrial gas turbine demand from data center buildout
further FY2026 guidance raises/beats at Aug 6 earnings

HEI.thesis: HEICO is compounding through a genuine demand inflection in both defense electronics and next-gen aircraft aftermarket parts, with record results, raised guidance, and rapidly rising price targets confirming durable share gains rather than a one-off beat.
